root_cause.text: The nft_bitwise shift implementation allows a zero shift operand, which causes the carry propagation logic to evaluate `BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - 0` as a 32-bit shift, an undefined behavior in C that can lead to incorrect processing or security vulnerabilities.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states, "The carry propagation logic computes the carry from the adjacent 32-bit word using BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - shift. A zero shift operand turns this into a 32-bit shift, which is undefined behaviour." The patch adds a check `!priv->data.data[0]` to reject zero shift values alongside the existing check for shifts >= 32, as seen in the diff: `if (!priv->data.data[0] || priv->data.data[0] >= BITS_PER_TYPE(u32))`.

candidates.rationale: This check only rejects shift amounts >= 32, but allows shift amount 0, which later causes undefined behavior in carry propagation when computing BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - shift.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition only rejects shift amounts >= 32 but allows a zero shift amount. Later, the carry propagation logic computes BITS_PER_TYPE(u32) - priv->data.data[0] = 32 - 0, which results in a 32-bit shift, an undefined behavior in C that can lead to security vulnerabilities.
